useCase.name: Record what an employee is paid, approve it before it takes effect, and keep every previous figure
useCase.featureRef: 12.16 Setting and changing an employee's salary

intent.name: salary.set
intent.summary: Record what an employee is paid, from when. One step, and it is not in force until it is approved.
routesHere: set her salary at 72,000 a month from the 1st of October

routesHere.text: in ki tankhwah 72,000 mahana, 1 October se
routesHere.gloss: set their salary at 72,000 a month from 1 October

routesHere.text: tankhwah record par darj kar do
routesHere.gloss: record the salary on the record

routesElsewhere.note: A change carries a reason and closes the previous figure at its effective date (BR-6, BR-10).
The daily rate is derived from the monthly amount rather than typed, so the two can never disagree (BR-3).
Payroll calculates from the figure in force for the month being run (BR-7).

steps.note: One step. It records a figure and puts nothing in force — a salary awaiting approval is not in force, and payroll finds no figure and does not pay on a proposal (BR-5).

plan.onFailure: Stop and report. No budget for the role, an effective date before joining, and an overlap with a figure already in force all arrive as errors.
plan.atomicity: One write: the salary row and the audit entry together or not at all. **Nothing is in force.** Payroll will find no figure for a month covered only by this until it is approved, and the employee is not paid on a proposal (BR-5). The daily rate is derived from the monthly amount rather than typed (BR-3).

parameters.name: monthly_amount
parameters.notes: The agreed monthly salary, greater than zero (E1), recorded against the budget set for the role (BR-2). What somebody is paid — never derived from the budget, from another employee, or from anything else.

parameters.name: effective_from
parameters.notes: The date the figure takes effect. May be in the future, so a rise agreed in June and effective in August is recorded once and takes effect by itself (BR-9). Not before the employee's joining date (E7).

parameters.name: branch_id
parameters.notes: Never from the request, even where the request names a campus or a past year (branch-scope, academic-session-scope).

fields.name: salary_id
fields.description: The salary record.

fields.name: monthly_amount
fields.description: As agreed. Visible only to the roles the visibility rule names (BR-8).

fields.name: daily_rate
fields.description: Derived from the monthly amount, not typed (BR-3). Payroll uses it to value a day.

fields.name: effective_from
fields.description: When it takes effect.

fields.name: role_salary_budget
fields.description: The budget set for the role, which the figure is recorded against (BR-2).

fields.name: exceeds_budget
fields.description: True where the agreed figure is above the budget for the role (A1). Recorded, not refused.

fields.name: status
fields.description: Draft. Not in force (BR-5).

errors.meaning: The monthly amount is zero or less.
No budget was set for the role.
errors.note: A figure agreed with no reference to a budget is a figure nobody planned for (BR-2).

errors.meaning: The effective date is before the employee's joining date.
The effective date overlaps a figure already in force.
errors.note: Two figures for the same employee may not have overlapping effective periods (BR-10).

errors.meaning: The acting role is configured to set the salary but cannot see the salary section.
errors.note: The two rules cannot both hold and the school has not decided (BR-11).

planningRules.rule: Never supply the amount. It is what a person is paid, and a figure taken from the role's budget, from a colleague, or from the appointment letter is the school agreeing a salary nobody agreed.
Never compute the daily rate. It is derived from the monthly amount so the two can never disagree (BR-3), and payroll values every absent day with it.
Never choose the effective date. It decides which months are paid at which figure (BR-7), and a date a planner picked changes what somebody was paid for a month already worked.
Report where the figure exceeds the role's budget. A1 records it rather than refusing it, and the approver should see it before they approve.
Say plainly that nothing is in force. Payroll finds no figure and does not pay on a proposal (BR-5) — an employee whose salary sits unapproved through a payroll run is not paid.
Never repeat the figure to an actor who may not see it. The salary and its history are visible only to the roles the visibility rule names (BR-8).

Report the visibility contradiction where the acting role cannot see the salary section. BR-11 states plainly that the rule making the School Admin unable to see any salary and this feature making them the one who sets it cannot both hold, and that the use case cannot be built correctly until the school decides. E10 is where it surfaces — report it as the documented conflict it is, not as a permissions error.

reversal.statement: A salary is never deleted (BR-12, E9) and a previous figure is never overwritten (BR-6, E8). A wrong figure is returned unapproved, or superseded by a new one with its own effective date.

resolvedPlans.outcome: Nothing is saved. Report this as the documented conflict it is (PR-7): the visibility rule says the School Admin cannot see any salary, this feature makes them the one who sets it, and the use case states outright that the two cannot both hold until the school decides which. It is not a permission to be granted quietly.
